A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TESSERA. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V5 reports original crop classification, canopy-height, biomass, fire-detection and stocking-index results, plus scaling and ablation experiments.

after.justification: V6 retains original downstream experiments and reports additional benchmark, ablation and temporal-robustness results.

M1.justification: The architecture, temporal sampling, quantization and displayed training objectives remain substantially unchanged. However, new Algorithm 1 specifies an unspecified Beta mixture and different mixup-loss scaling, while Section 3.3 retains v5's uniform mixture and objective. The PDFs do not establish whether these differences represent a method change or inconsistent pseudocode.

E1.justification: V6 adds German tree-species classification on TreeSatAI-TS and French parcel segmentation on PASTIS-R. It removes the California wildfire and Brazilian agroforestry stocking-index studies, including their appendices. Austrian crop, Finnish biomass and Borneo canopy-height coverage remains.

E2.justification: Table 1 substantially expands comparisons on retained biomass and canopy-height tasks, adding models such as CROMA, DOFA, Galileo and SkySense, plus UNet and ViT baselines. The canopy-product comparison loses ETH, GLAD and the regional CHM. Meta Global CHM is retained under the name DINOv2 Global CHM, not added as a new comparator.

E3.justification: V6 adds frozen-encoder versus full-finetuning comparisons and evaluations at 1%, 30% and full label availability across its benchmark suite. New analyses vary temporal sampling, seasonal inclusion, finetuning schedules and regional training. These extend the evaluation design; the main pretraining configuration remains unchanged. Newly documented Austrian split construction alone does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V6 adds a no-pretraining ablation, cloud-observation sensitivity, encoder-finetuning and regional-retraining comparisons, temporal-resampling analysis, a timestep accuracy–speed sweep and seasonal exclusion tests (Table 3, Figure 6, Tables 5 and 8). The earlier projector-scaling and shuffling/mixup/Sentinel-1/quantization ablations are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Figure 6d newly reports empirical performance distributions across random temporal draws, without specifying their count. The earlier twelve-model canopy evaluation and five-split biomass reporting remain. The retained crop few-shot figure's caption becomes less precise, replacing the explicit standard-deviation description with generic variation over runs.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports substantial additional results, including full-label TreeSatAI-TS F1 of 77.96 versus AlphaEarth's 76.90 and PASTIS-R mIoU of 50.68 versus 51.08. New ablation and robustness outcomes are also reported, while fire, stocking-index and several canopy-product results disappear. Table 1's Borneo RMSE of 12.21 m does not replace the retained 8.88 m result in Figure 16; their settings are insufficiently reconciled for a direct performance-change claim.

T1.justification: The d-pixel definitions, displayed Barlow-Twins and mixup equations, RankMe definition and clustering-metric formulas are retained or relocated. Added encoder expressions restate previously described operations. No new theorem, proof or substantive theoretical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains open, global, 10 m embeddings with strong label efficiency. V6 adds specific introductory claims about consistency under shifted calendars and missing seasons, while dropping the fire-detection and carbon-market application claims. Much of the remaining contribution wording is reframing rather than a new scientific claim.

C2.justification: V6 adds interpretations about cloud-sparsity limits, negligible benefits from finetuning or regional retraining, and winter observations introducing noise. It also removes comparison caveats concerning biomass input differences and local versus global canopy models. V5's explicit warning about increasing high-biomass bias becomes a claim of minimal bias across biomass ranges, despite the retained Figure 5 showing substantial high-value underestimation.

D1.justification: V6 adds mixup/shuffling pseudocode, Austrian field and spatial split construction, downstream head specifications, and inference hardware and data-volume information. Conversely, it removes v5's Pooch checksum/versioning and Parquet-index instructions, along with explicit Sen2Cor/SNAP preprocessing disclosures. The principal architecture and pretraining hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Sections 2 and A.1 substantially develop positioning around temporal irregularity, embedding-based access and usability, including a visual-foundation-model/vision-language-model taxonomy. Newly discussed and cited work includes SatCLIP, GeoRSCLIP, EarthGPT and SkySenseGPT. Extensive application-specific literature is removed, while the broad foundation-model comparison table is retained.

P1.justification: V6 rewrites the title, abstract and introduction, replaces lengthy application narratives with benchmark-oriented experiment sections, and adds dedicated Related Work and Discussion sections. Definitions and losses move into the main text, while the appendices are extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: The document changes to a two-column layout with substantially redesigned displays. V6 adds a benchmark table, robustness panels, taxonomy diagram, observation maps and several specification/ablation tables. The crop figure is split across main text and appendix, the canopy comparison shrinks from eight panels to four, and fire and stocking-index figures disappear.

improvement.justification: Table 1's broader comparisons and the new temporal-robustness studies address important evidential gaps in v5. However, v6 leaves new and retained canopy results insufficiently reconciled, introduces conflicting mixup descriptions in Section 3.3 and Algorithm 1, and overstates biomass accuracy relative to its retained Figure 5. The gains in experimental breadth coexist with material losses in consistency and interpretation, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
